title: Platform tool-pin catalog, schema_version 2
description: Documents adoption/pins-linux-x86_64.json (and any later adoption/pins-<platform>.json migrated to schema_version 2). This is a documentation/reference schema only: adoption/bootstrap-linux.sh reads pins with jq and does not validate against this file; adoption/tools/ecosystem-switch reads the per-tool switch fields (root_name, current_link, entrypoints, surfaces, state_dirs, window, rollback_class) as its component spec when given --pins/--spec pointing at a file shaped like this. scripts/validate.py's pins-v2 parity check (validate_pins_v2) implements the cross-file rules below directly in stdlib Python, not by loading this file with a JSON Schema library; tests/test_pins_v2.py keeps the two in sync structurally. A component whose real value could not be independently verified during migration carries a nested {"status": "pending", ...} object instead of a fabricated value for that one field; validate_pins_v2 treats those report-only, never a hard failure, per switch.md's 'unknown fields for other winners can be filled later by the qualify wave (mark pending)'.

schema_version.description: adoption/pins-<platform>.json files not yet migrated from schema_version 1 have no candidates/supersedes/divergence sections and only the legacy per-tool fields (id, version, kind, url, sha256, install_note).

schema_v2_note.description: Free-text migration provenance; not read by any script.

candidates.description: Installable winners named elsewhere in the catalog (a layer's winners[] or a Facts section naming a hard-coded root) that have no url/sha256 pin in this file yet. Never a hard-failure source for scripts/validate.py; always report-only.

supersedes.description: Other, out-of-repository version records this file is now the reference over (switch.md Facts: 'Version records disagree'). Each entry is provenance (a path and a sha256 read once, for the record) and is never edited to match -- the host files themselves are outside every worktree.

divergence.description: Declared, intentional mismatches between this file's install pin and the version another manifest (manifests/stack.json, a catalogs/landscape/*.json winner) cites as evidence -- for example a self-updating native binary whose install floor keeps moving ahead of the version any recorded task actually ran against. scripts/validate.py's parity check reads this array by id and does not fail that one id's mismatch while it stays declared here.

id.description: Must match a tools[].id in this same file.

pendingField.description: In place of any field below, an object {"status": "pending", "note": text} defers that one value to a later qualify wave instead of guessing it.

bin.description: ECO_INSTALL_ROOT-relative path of the symlink or launcher that resolves this executable today, e.g. "bin/node".

in_root.description: Path of the real executable relative to this tool's root_name (tools/<root_name>/<in_root>), or null when the component has no switch-managed root (see rollback_class not_applicable).

old.description: text-replace only: the literal old substring adopt --relink looks for (defaults to this tool's real, resolved root_name path). Refused unless it occurs exactly expected_count times; refused outright when path contains '/frozen/'. A second relink that finds old_text already fully replaced (and the new current/<id> text already present) treats the surface as already migrated and leaves it unchanged, rather than refusing (adopt --relink is idempotent).

expected_pre_sha256.description: text-replace only, optional: sha256 of the target's exact current bytes, checked before any write (adoption/tools/ecosystem-switch's op_text_replace expected_pre_sha256 parameter) so a surface that drifted from what this pin was written against is refused rather than blindly rewritten. Omitted entries (the default so far) skip this precondition and rely on the old-substring-count check alone.

content_utf8.description: file-write only: the UTF-8 text adopt --relink writes at path, backing up any pre-existing file first.

id.description: Stable component id; matches manifests/stack.json components[].id where the component is also catalog-tracked.

sha256.description: Exactly one of sha256 or lock_ref must be present and non-null; adoption/bootstrap-linux.sh's install_pin refuses a null sha256 (fail closed).

lock_ref.description: Alternative to sha256 for a pin whose upstream installer resolves and verifies its own lock (e.g. a uv-tool kind resolved from PyPI by uv itself); names the lock mechanism instead of duplicating a hash uv does not check.

bin.description: native kind only: the command name the self-installing binary's own installer creates.

root_name.description: tools/<root_name> under ECO_INSTALL_ROOT holds this version's real, immutable install; null (with rollback_class not_applicable) when the kind has no such discrete root (native, or a uv-tool kind whose environment uv itself owns).

current_link.description: The current/<id> switch point ecosystem-switch flips to change this component's active root_name; null exactly when root_name is null.

window.description: Name of a switch/windows/<name>.json this component's apply/unit-restart operations are gated by.

divergence_ref.description: id of a divergence[] entry (usually this same tool's id) that documents why this pin intentionally differs from another manifest's cited version.
